entries.note: The agent menu and the open chooser are file-scope here rather than fields on ReApp because one window draws one Tasks surface at a time and one row has a chooser open at a time, nothing outside this file reads either, and fixed arrays mean nothing is owned that a close path would have to free. The menu carries the root it answered for: a second Tasks tab on another project must not inherit this one's agent list, so every use is behind menu_answers(tab root) and a chooser opened before the answer says "Reading the agent menu" rather than listing another project's CLIs. The kinds are mutually exclusive by construction: chooser_toggle writes one `kind` and one `task`, so opening Tests on a row closes a Spawn chooser open elsewhere. That is deliberate — two open blocks would each claim to describe "the" task, which is the confusion the inline layout exists to prevent.

entries.note: The chooser draws as rows under its task instead of as an overlay for three reasons, in order of weight: an overlay costs one of microui's 32 root containers, which fifteen leaf panes with a surface open already fill (the same budget that keeps the token segment out of microui); a chooser that scrolls with its row cannot end up describing a different task than the one under it; and the pane is already a scrolled list, so nothing about the layer is gained. The row's control cluster reserves its columns by negative width the way the trailing pill does -- a leading -1 would fill to the right edge and push everything after it out of the pane (5a0bc38). F115 (spec 116) adds a third kind, RE_CHOOSER_TESTS, drawing the task's claims and the evidence that backs them; it follows this rule for the same three reasons rather than becoming the popover the other two refused to be. Its Tests caret is drawn on EVERY row, including a provider that answers with an empty evidence list, because an absent control reads as "this task has no tests" rather than "this provider cannot say" — so its column is reserved unconditionally, unlike Decompose and Hold token which are local-only. That rendering choice is not covered by the native suite (KI-073): every row the harness can reach comes from a local provider, so gating the caret on `local` leaves the suite green. A fourth kind, RE_CHOOSER_DETAILS (spec 119), is opened by the TITLE rather than by a caret of its own: the row trims the title, so the thing that was cut is the thing you click, and a row already carrying four controls and a pill gains no column. It is the one kind that uses re_ui_paragraph, because a trimmed acceptance criterion is worthless. Its layout answers to design/previews/views/tasks.html rather than to taste: inset by the key column with a rail so the block belongs to its row, one value column under right-aligned kickers, numbered criteria, and no repeated key or spacer rows. Change the card first; native-design.spec.mjs asserts against the measurements design.py generates from it.

entries.note: The worker advertises agentsMenu always but agentSpawn and taskWrites only where it owns the ledger (spec 095's asymmetry: a caller is refused by name rather than reaching a worker with no gate). So the pane refuses locally and names the missing prerequisite instead of posting into a 404. Decompose has the stricter gate of the two because its only legitimate output is task_add calls, and a worker that cannot write the inventory has nowhere to put the subtasks it would produce. Refusals land in menu.note, drawn as a row of the pane and reported as `tracker-note`: the worker's own refusals name a whole prerequisite (a session host predating task-driven panes) that a 512-byte status line truncates, and its `detail` -- started, retained, could not be shown -- must not read as an error to retry.

Measured before it was written (spec 120): with ~/nolf-improved's 1317 tasks the tab emitted 35 213 draw commands a frame against 842 after, because every row was laid out, had its full description measured by re_draw_text_width, and became draw commands that microui then clipped away. The cost was O(inventory) to show about twenty rows.

The adaptation of React Native's VirtualizedList drops its hardest part. That list must estimate row heights and correct once it has measured them, because it builds a retained tree before laying it out; here rows are emitted in order, so after a spacer `layout->next_row` IS the content offset of the row about to be drawn. The window is computed from truth every frame — nothing is estimated and nothing needs correcting.

Two things a later editor will be tempted to simplify and must not. A run of skipped rows becomes ONE spacer of the run's exact height minus one style->spacing (the layout adds a spacing after every row); drop that and content_size shrinks, so the scrollbar reports the viewport rather than the list. And the row named by menu.task is always emitted even when it is outside the window, because an open chooser's block is far taller than its row and reaches into the viewport when the row does not — without the exception, scrolling a detail block half off the top makes it disappear.

The regression asserts the draw list stays flat as the inventory grows AND that the visible rows are pixel-identical between a 200-row and a 1300-row list: a window that drew the wrong rows would pass a command count and fail the pixels.
